records.title: Programming 1
records.summary: Introduces C programming, control flow, software design, memory management, and elementary data structures. Provides a foundation for further programming study.

rule.note: Resolve and review enrollment requirement reference 019404 before evaluating eligibility.

records.learning_note: Programming foundations support both directions. Use this to build confidence with C, control flow, and memory before more specialized study.

records.title: Fundamentals of Computer Organization
records.summary: Examines processor organization, instruction sets, memory and caches, and computer-design trade-offs. Uses MIPS and reduced-instruction-set examples to connect software with hardware behavior.

rule.note: Resolve and review enrollment requirement reference 016494 before evaluating eligibility.

records.learning_note: Understanding processor instructions, memory, and caches provides a bridge from programming to embedded hardware.

records.title: Microprocessor Organization
records.summary: Studies microcontrollers and hardware interfaces through C programming, interrupts, timers, serial communication, and analog conversion. Includes laboratories and a project using a microcontroller platform.

rule.note: Resolve and review enrollment requirement reference 016495 before evaluating eligibility.

records.learning_note: Microcontroller programming and hardware interfaces connect an embedded-systems goal with practical device projects. Prepare programming and processor foundations first.

records.title: Introduction to Deep Learning: An Engineering Perspective
records.summary: Introduces neural-network principles, optimization, and engineering applications. Covers perceptrons, convolutional and attention models, and methods for efficient model training and inference.

rule.note: Resolve and review enrollment requirement reference 019593 before evaluating eligibility.

records.learning_note: Neural-network principles and engineering applications connect to an AI/ML goal. Treat this as a later goal until the relevant academic preparation and enrollment requirements are confirmed.

records.title: Introduction to Computer Programming II
records.summary: Develops programming and problem-solving skills through data structures and their implementations. Topics include lists, stacks, queues, trees, searching, sorting, and exceptions.
records.learning_note: Data structures connect introductory programming with the software skills used in later AI work. Check the recorded grade requirement before considering enrollment.

records.title: PyTorch Quickstart
records.summary: Practice a basic deep learning workflow with data loading, neural-network construction, optimization, and saved model parameters. A useful hands-on companion to introductory neural-network coursework.
records.learning_note: Use this to connect Python programming with a small deep learning workflow after building programming foundations.
records.first_activity: Work through loading data and running the example model. Note how the training and evaluation steps differ.

records.title: CS50 — Introduction to Computer Science
records.summary: Build programming foundations through C, algorithms, memory, and data structures, then progress to Python and web topics. OpenCourseWare provides material for independent study.
records.learning_note: Use this alongside programming foundations when you want guided practice outside university coursework.
records.first_activity: Start with the introduction and its first exercise. Move through the material at your own pace.

records.title: AI and machine learning
records.summary: Team learning connection: neural-network coursework and practical PyTorch exercises can support an interest in AI and machine learning. Programming and data-structure foundations provide supporting skills. This is a suggested learning direction, not a hiring or degree guarantee.

records.title: Embedded systems
records.summary: Team learning connection: C programming, processor architecture, microcontrollers, and hardware interfaces form a useful learning direction for embedded systems. A course match indicates relevant study rather than proven job eligibility.
